concepts.title: How Do Plants Grow?
concepts.definition: Plants grow from tiny seeds into great trees without eating anything, which puzzled thinkers for ages; experiments testing soil, water and weight showed that plants are not simply soil-eaters.
concepts.key_idea: A plant's mass comes mostly from air and water, not from the soil it stands in.

concepts.title: Photosynthesis: Making Food from Light
concepts.definition: Green leaves are food factories: chlorophyll traps sunlight and uses its energy to combine water from the soil with carbon dioxide from air, making glucose and releasing oxygen, the process called photosynthesis.
concepts.formula: carbon dioxide + water + sunlight = glucose + oxygen
concepts.key_idea: Photosynthesis feeds nearly all life: leaves cook the food on which animals also dine.

concepts.title: Transport in Plants
concepts.definition: Plants run their own plumbing: roots absorb water and minerals, thin tubes called xylem lift the water up the stem, and phloem carries prepared food to every part, driven by transpiration's pull from the leaves.
concepts.key_idea: Two pipelines, one upward and one all-around: xylem raises water, phloem distributes food.

concepts.title: Do Plants Respire?
concepts.definition: Plants breathe too: day and night they take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide while burning food for energy, and at night, without photosynthesis to mask it, gas exchange through stomata shows respiration clearly.
concepts.formula: glucose + oxygen = energy + carbon dioxide + water
concepts.key_idea: Photosynthesis and respiration run opposite ways: one stores sunlight in food, the other spends it.
